idiom_name: limits strategies (Redis/Memcached/memory) as the substrate, slowapi or flask-limiter as the web adapter
implementation_notes: Python ships no rate limiter in the standard library, so the pattern comes from the limits package: fixed-window, moving-window and sliding-window-counter strategies with identical APIs for sync and async code over Redis, Memcached or in-memory storage. Web frameworks sit on top of it - slowapi adapts limits to Starlette/FastAPI with a @limiter.limit('5/minute') decorator and a 429 handler, flask-limiter does the same for Flask - and the in-memory backend is only correct for a single worker process. A dependency-free token bucket is a short hand-rolled function over time.monotonic(); asyncio.Semaphore bounds concurrency, never rate.
pitfalls: In-memory storage is per worker process: with several gunicorn/uvicorn workers the effective limit is multiplied; point storage_uri at Redis or Memcached.
Decorator order matters and the endpoint must take the request argument explicitly, or the limiter cannot identify the caller (slowapi documents both).
A hand-rolled bucket over time.time() breaks on NTP steps - time.monotonic() is the interval clock and time.monotonic_ns avoids float drift.
